comments.author: armanboyaci
comments.why: Advocates simulation and shuffling over memorizing formulas
comments.text: >Being able to apply statistics is like having a secret superpower. I totally with this sentence. BUT If you ask for my opinion, merely knowing a list of statistical formulas is not very helpful. Most of the time, people don’t remember the underlying assumptions, so there is a fair chance they will use them in inappropriate situations. I recommend watching these two YouTube videos. The presenters advocate using simulation/bootstrapping/shuffling methods instead of memorizing formulas. Jake Vanderplas - Statistics for Hackers [LINK] John Rauser - Statistics Without the Agonizing Pain [VIDEO]
